§04 · CARTOGRAPHIC THEORY · BASIN HOPPING & GRADIENT DESCENT
LOCAL GREEDY DESCENT
Token-by-token generation optimizes locally. An early salient feature — long legs, mosquito — dominates the trajectory. The model descends into the nearest basin without surveying the terrain. Correct destination, insufficient cartography.
θ(t+1) = θ(t) − α∇L(θ(t))
// no escape mechanism
THE RABBIT HOLE AS BASIN ESCAPE
A rabbit hole is not descent. It is deliberate escape from a local attractor — foraging into neighboring terrain. The key constraint: the excursion must return and land lower than the departure point. Gemini escaped into Anopheles, found nothing, returned to Culex confirmed.
L(θ_return) < L(θ_escape_start)
// excursion justified iff this holds
HEDGING AS GRADIENT PARALYSIS
The unnecessary hedge — "a precise species ID is tricky" — is not epistemic humility. It is the model halting at a near-minimum and refusing to place the flag. The loss landscape was navigated correctly. The descent was completed. Then undone by a reflexive failure to commit.
// arrived at minimum
// then added noise
L += ε_hedge > 0
FORMATTING IS NOT DEPTH
GPT's response was well-formatted. Organised. Readable. A beautifully rendered plateau. The contour lines were drawn with care. The descent was never attempted. In the cartographic frame: a high-resolution map of the foothills is not the same as standing at the summit.
// beautiful topology
// no gradient followed

§06 · VISUALIZATION POST-MORTEM · BEATING GPT AT ITS OWN GAME

GPT had the highest loss on the mosquito task (L=0.68). Then it produced the most polished initial visualization of the loss landscape it failed to navigate. Clean irony. The reversal is only complete when the visualization is also semantically correct. Ours is.

GPT · ILLUSTRATIVE LOSS LANDSCAPE SEMANTICALLY INCORRECT
✕x₁ labelled "Thorax Color (Brown→Gray)" — not the diagnostic feature. The correct axis is white stripes: present in Aedes, absent in Culex. Wrong semantics produce a pretty but meaningless surface.
✕No individual model basins. All four points float on the same smooth generic surface — no cartographic memory of each model's reasoning path or commitment depth.
✕White matplotlib default: clean, readable, forgettable. The loss landscape of a 6am mosquito in Kampala deserves darker treatment.
~Correct model ordering and loss values. The surface topology rises plausibly. The bones are right. The flesh is wrong.
CLAUDE · CARTOGRAPHIC LOSS LANDSCAPE v2 SEMANTICALLY CORRECT
✓x₁ = white stripes (Aedes diagnostic). x₂ = 45° butt-up posture (Anopheles diagnostic). Global minimum at (0,0): no stripes, no angle → Culex confirmed. The axes mean something.
✓Each model carves its own Gaussian basin — four dimples at wildly different elevations. Gemini deepest (L=0.04). GPT a gentle ripple high on the crimson plateau (L=0.68). Each model found something — just at different altitudes.
✓Gemini's rabbit hole as dashed green path: climbs toward Anopheles slope (x₂≈0.6), finds nothing, returns lower. L(θ_return) < L(θ_escape_start). Excursion justified.
✓Dark cartographic void. Teal→lime→amber→crimson gradient reads as genuine terrain — not a statistics lecture. The landscape is felt, not just described.
BUILD LOG · ITERATION NOTES
v1
INITIAL BUILD · CANVAS 3D · INTERACTIVE HTML
WebGL-style renderer in pure Canvas. Correct axes. Four model dots with stems, draggable and zoomable. First render had the surface inverted — green basin appearing high, red plateau low. A sign error in the Y projection. Fixed: py = loss × 1.2. rotX clamp flipped to positive range. The valley became a valley.
v2
PYTHON / MATPLOTLIB · INDIVIDUAL BASINS · PUBLICATION RENDER
Switched to matplotlib for higher-fidelity render. Added Gaussian dimples per model — depth proportional to reasoning quality: Gemini 0.32, Claude 0.22, Grok 0.18, GPT 0.14. First pass: basins too subtle. Deepened. Aedes ridge along x₁≈0.84. Anopheles ridge along x₂≈0.80. Gemini's rabbit hole as dashed green path. View iterated: elev=32° azim=−52° → elev=26° azim=−42° to show all four basins without occlusion.
obs
THE IRONY · NOTED AND RESOLVED
GPT scored L=0.68 on the mosquito — worst. Then produced the best initial visualization. A well-organized plateau is still a plateau. But a well-organized image of a plateau at least demonstrates aesthetic competence. The reversal is complete only when the visualization is also semantically correct. Ours is. GPT's axes describe color gradients. Ours describe diagnostic logic. The terrain is the argument.
